query: Classify neurons from all 3 fish into molecular subtypes based on combinatorial expression of 41 genes. Display a gene expression heatmap with neurons ordered by subtype identity, alongside a subtype color vector and a brain region annotation vector, showing how unique gene combinations define subtypes and how subtypes map to  anatomical locations.

analyse_plan.Objective: Classify neurons into molecular subtypes using binary gene expression profiles (41 genes), ensure subtype replicability across three fish via strict filtering criteria, and visualize the relationship between gene expression, molecular subtypes, and anatomical location.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Confirm that 41 genes (including cfos) are included in the expression matrix. Verify that molecular subtypes meet cross-animal replication criteria: present in all 3 fish, ≥5 cells per fish per brain region, and no single fish contributes >70% of cells per subtype. Ensure brain region annotations are consistent with the mapZebrain atlas. Validate that cells are binned every 10 cells for visualization without distorting patterns.
analyse_plan.Steps:
1. Load Data: Import RNA spot counts for 41 genes, brain region annotations, and cell segmentation data from three main experimental fish.
2. Cell Filtering: Select cells positive for at least one gene (excluding cfos for subtype classification) and located in functionally imaged planes.
3. Binary Gene Expression: Binarize RNA spot counts using gene-specific thresholds (default 25 spots, adjusted via Maximum Deviation for variable-expression genes) to create a "neurons × genes" binary matrix.
4. Subtype Classification: Identify unique gene expression combinations (barcoding) as molecular subtypes, applying filtering criteria for cross-animal replication (present in all 3 fish, ≥5 cells per fish, ≥2 neighbors within 40 μm).
5. Data Binning: Bin cells every 10 rows for clarity; use mode for categorical variables (molecular subtypes, brain regions) and average for gene expression spot counts.
6.Save Key Results: Save the raw binarized 41-gene expression matrix, molecular subtype label vector (332 subtypes), brain region annotation vector, binned gene expression heatmap matrix, binned molecular subtype color vector, binned brain region color vector, subtype-to-color mapping dictionary, brain-region-to-color mapping dictionary, gene list and vertical grouping guide line coordinates (red/black dashed lines), per-subtype cell count statistics, and binning parameter (bin_size=10 cells).
7. Visualization: Generate a layered matrix visualization displaying binned gene expression profiles (41 genes), molecular subtype labels (332 total), and brain region annotations, with consistent color coding for subtypes across figures.

statistical_info.number: 41 genes total; 40 used for subtype classification (excluding cfos)

key_analysis_results: Across three fish, 332 molecular subtypes are identified based on unique combinations of 41 genes (including cfos), with subtypes ranging from single-gene positive to 5-gene co-expressing. The visualization shows binned gene expression profiles, subtype classifications, and brain region assignments, with all subtypes validated to be present in all three fish and meeting cell count/neighborhood criteria.
key_analysis_conclusions: The cross-animal validated molecular subtype classification provides a standardized framework for linking gene expression to anatomy and function, enabling consistent comparison of neuronal populations across individuals and experiments.

summary_report.abstract: Fig_3B visualizes cross-animal molecular subtype classification: 332 validated molecular subtypes (from unique 41-gene expression combinations) are displayed alongside binned gene expression profiles and brain region annotations for three fish, with subtypes meeting strict replication criteria (present in all fish, ≥5 cells per fish, no single-fish dominance), establishing a standardized gene-based neuronal classification.
summary_report.methods: Data for Fig_3B came from three main experimental Tg(elavl3:H2B-GCaMP7f) zebrafish larvae (6 dpf), with RNA spot counts for 41 genes measured via EASI-FISH and brain region annotations from registration to the mapZebrain atlas. Cells were filtered to include those positive for at least one gene (excluding cfos for subtype classification) and located in functionally imaged planes. RNA spot counts were binarized using gene-specific thresholds (default 25 spots; adjusted via Maximum Deviation for genes with variable expression). Unique gene expression combinations (barcoding) were classified as molecular subtypes, with filtering for cross-animal replication: presence in all 3 fish, ≥5 cells per fish per brain region, ≥2 neighbors within 40 μm, and no single fish contributing >70% of cells per subtype. Cells were binned every 10 rows for visualization (mode for categorical variables, average for gene expression). The visualization includes a binned gene expression matrix (41 genes), molecular subtype labels (332 total), and brain region annotations, with subtype color coding using distinctipy for uniqueness.
summary_report.results: The visualization displays a binned matrix of RNA spot counts for 41 genes (including cfos) across neurons from three fish, with rows binned every 10 cells for clarity. A vertical vector indicates molecular subtype classification (332 total), with subtypes ranging from single-gene positive (40 subtypes) to 5-gene co-expressing (4 subtypes). Another vertical vector shows brain region annotations (16 main regions, e.g., Pal, OT, Cb, SupMO), revealing spatial clustering of specific subtypes. All subtypes are present in all three fish, with no single fish contributing >70% of cells for any subtype, confirming cross-animal replicability. Gene expression patterns show partial overlap across subtypes, as designed to identify cell subtypes with distinct molecular profiles.
summary_report.discussion: Fig_3B establishes the core molecular classification framework for the study, addressing a key challenge in systems neuroscience: standardizing neuronal cell types across individuals. The 332 cross-animal validated molecular subtypes provide a granular, reproducible way to group neurons by gene expression, moving beyond single-gene markers to multi-gene co-expression profiles. The strict filtering criteria (present in all fish, cell count thresholds, neighborhood requirements) ensure that subtypes represent biologically meaningful populations rather than technical artifacts. By linking subtypes to brain region annotations, the visualization reveals spatial patterning of molecular identity—critical for understanding how gene expression shapes regional circuit function. This classification serves as the foundation for subsequent analyses (e.g., subtype-specific activity responses, behavior correlations), enabling consistent comparison of neuronal populations across the three fish and facilitating high-throughput function-to-gene mapping. The binned visualization balances detail and readability, making it feasible to present data from hundreds of thousands of cells while highlighting key patterns in gene expression and subtype distribution.

question: ﻿To visualize the classification of neurons from all 3 fish into molecular subtypes based on combinatorial gene expression profiles. A heatmap of RNA transcript spot counts for 41 genes was plotted for all neurons from the 3 fish ordered by molecular subtype identity, alongside a subtype color vector and a brain region vector, where all vectors and matrices were binned every 10 cells for clarity, with the gene expression matrix binned every 130 cells using the first cell per group.
